Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

You are an adversarial verifier. A finder claims this is LEGACY code safe to delete. Try hard to REFUTE it.

Finding: repo=andesim path=driver/hotloops.cpp lines=741-747 kind=legacy-fallback
Claim: The hotloops driver's default plugin path is build/qemu/contrib/plugins/libhotloops.so, the removed in-tree-QEMU build location; the plugin now builds at qemu_plugin/libhotloops.so, so the documented `build/hotloops <elf>` flow fails on a clean checkout unless --plugin is passed.
Evidence given: hotloops.cpp:744-746 is the ONLY default (no qemu_plugin/ candidate). qemu_plugin/Makefile builds libhotloops.so 'in this directory'; scripts/hotloops.sh:121 already defaults to ${ROOT}/qemu_plugin/libhotloops.so; scripts/build_all.sh:52-53 documents the same. QEMU/ submodule is gone (git ls-files | grep '^QEMU/' = 0 hits); build/ is gitignored and build/qemu on this machine is a stale leftover whose symlinks dangle to the deleted /home/nick/work/andesim/QEMU. docs/USER_GUIDE.md:683,692 tells users to run build/hotloops, which hits this broken default. Lines 728-730 have the same build/qemu fallback for the QEMU binary (QEMU_BIN_DIR is at least tried first there).

Repo roots: andesim=/home/nick/work/andesim, vsim=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim.
Checks you MUST do:
1. Read the file/lines yourself — does the claim match reality?
2. grep BOTH repos (tracked files) for references: filename, function names, symbols, script names, make targets, cmake targets, doc links.
3. Check tests/e2e.sh, scripts/*, Makefiles, CMake, and CLAUDE.md/docs for indirect usage (variable-built names, glob patterns like test_*.sh runners).
4. git log --follow -5 on the file: was it recently touched for a live feature?
5. Is it an INTENTIONAL fallback/compat layer per CLAUDE.md (e.g. semihost_exit.inc)?

- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_all.sh -- build the andesim artifacts. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim build` subcommand (which moved out of the driver
# binary). It only orchestrates the existing build scripts / Makefiles; the
# build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
#
# TARGET (default: all):
#   all       setup.sh (locate external qemu + vsim + plugin) then
#             fixtures (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib too)
#   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
#   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
#   runtime   build/runtime/ (rv64) + build/runtime/rv32/ (rv32, when
#             HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set): libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o,
#             andesim.ld, andesim.specs, include/andesim/ROI.h
#
# --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
#
# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

TARGET=all
DRY_RUN=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    all|plugin|fixtures|runtime) TARGET="$arg" ;;
    *)
      echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|plugin|fixtures|runtime] [--dry-run]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

# run one step: print it under --dry-run, otherwise banner + execute (inheriting
# stdio so the user watches the build live). set -e aborts on the first failure.
run() {
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$*"
    return
  fi
  printf '[build_all] %s\n' "$*"
  "$@"
}

# plugin: build_qemu_plugin.sh wraps `make -C qemu_plugin`; plugins build against
# the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h (no QEMU source tree needed).
case "$TARGET" in
  all)      run bash "$ROOT/setup.sh"; run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  plugin)   run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh" ;;
  fixtures) run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  runtime)  run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_runtime.sh" ;;
esac

#             andesim.ld, andesim.specs, include/andesim/ROI.h
#
# --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
#
# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

TARGET=all
DRY_RUN=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    all|plugin|fixtures|runtime) TARGET="$arg" ;;
    *)
      echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|plugin|fixtures|runtime] [--dry-run]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

# run one step: print it under --dry-run, otherwise banner + execute (inheriting
# stdio so the user watches the build live). set -e aborts on the first failure.
run() {
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$*"
    return
  fi
  printf '[build_all] %s\n' "$*"
  "$@"
}

# plugin: build_qemu_plugin.sh wraps `make -C qemu_plugin`; plugins build against
# the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h (no QEMU source tree needed).
case "$TARGET" in
  all)      run bash "$ROOT/setup.sh"; run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  plugin)   run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh" ;;
  fixtures) run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  runtime)  run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_runtime.sh" ;;
esac

# --- arch detection ---
if [[ "$ARCH" == "auto" ]]; then
    file_out="$(file -L -- "$ELF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$file_out" in
        *"ELF 64-bit"*"RISC-V"*)  ARCH=riscv64 ;;
        *"ELF 32-bit"*"RISC-V"*)  ARCH=riscv32 ;;
        *) echo "error: cannot auto-detect arch (not RISC-V?), pass --arch" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
fi

# --- locate qemu + plugin ---
# QEMU is an externally-built binary: QEMU_BIN_DIR (config.env, exported by
# setup.sh) holds qemu-system-{riscv32,riscv64}. The plugin builds out-of-tree
# under qemu_plugin/ (make -C qemu_plugin), never into QEMU.
if [[ -z "$QEMU" ]]; then
    QEMU="${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/build/qemu}/qemu-system-${ARCH}"
fi
[[ -x "$QEMU" ]] || { echo "error: qemu not found/executable: $QEMU" >&2; exit 2; }

if [[ -z "$PLUGIN" ]]; then
    PLUGIN="${ROOT}/qemu_plugin/libhotloops.so"
fi
[[ -f "$PLUGIN" ]] || { echo "error: plugin not built: $PLUGIN (run: make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT=\$PWD/QEMU)" >&2; exit 2; }

# --- run ---
# Temp files are declared up front so one EXIT trap covers every exit path,
# including the early --raw exit before SYMS/LINES/DISASM are created.
LOG="$(mktemp -t hotloops.XXXXXX.log)"
SYMS="" LINES="" DISASM=""
trap 'rm -f "$LOG" "$SYMS" "$LINES" "$DISASM"' EXIT

QEMU_CMD=("$QEMU"
          -plugin "${PLUGIN},limit=${LIMIT},min_iters=${MIN_ITERS}"
          -d plugin -D "$LOG"
          -M "$MACHINE"
          -cpu "$CPU"
          -nographic -semihosting
          -bios "$ELF")
[[ -n "$QEMU_CONFIG" ]] && QEMU_CMD+=(-readconfig "$QEMU_CONFIG")
[[ ${#EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS[@]} -gt 0 ]] && QEMU_CMD+=("${EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS[@]}")
---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the out-of-tree QEMU TCG plugins under qemu_plugin/:
#   libhybrid_handoff.so  -- hybrid QEMU<->vsim handoff plugin (product)
#   libhotloops.so        -- hot inner-loop detector (developer profiling tool)
#
# Thin wrapper over qemu_plugin/Makefile. The plugins build against the vendored
# qemu-plugin.h under qemu_plugin/include/, so NO QEMU source tree is needed --
# only the externally-built qemu-system-* binary is integrated at run time.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh [make-target...]   # e.g. clean, libhotloops.so
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

exec make -C "$ROOT/qemu_plugin" "$@"
